text.p: Copper firmed but gold eased in overnight trading but other base metals lanquished.
Wheat closed mixed with a new low set on the March contract while oil prices eased on ample supplies.
The CRB index eased 0.6 point to 238.63.
Copper prices pushed higher during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, regaining the $2,200 level to end the session firmer and geared up for Wednesday's Feb option declarations.
Other metals did not fare so well, particularly aluminium which came in for late technical selling, while Monday's star performers nickel and zinc opted for consolidation.
Business in the complex was fairly routine throughout the session, traders said.
In copper, the 8,750-tonne stock increase was shrugged off, as inventory rises are being factored in while the current high backwardation persists.
Nearby prompts remain tight, with cash/one day at $22.50 this afternoon, while an influx of borrowing to the Feb date helped arrest a softening trend in premiums and underpin the forward market.
Some resistance was again evident above $2,200, although the close at $2,204, $17 from Monday, was construed constructively on the charts.

Aluminium was unable to make headway above $1,625, despite the 7,500-tonne stock fall, and prices lost ground on late chartist selling. Final business was at $1,617.50, down $8.50, with a test of $1,600/10 likely now.

Nickel prices took a breather, following the sharp run-up seen in recent sessions which culminated in the market hitting 4-1/2 month highs on Monday. The 114-tonne stock increase also cautioned the market, although speculative interest is expected to resume on the upside.
Last trade was at $7,675 a tonne, down just $5 from the overnight kerb close.

Zinc similarly settled for a session of holding fire just under the two-year peaks of Monday, with stiff resistance likely from the mid-$1,170s up to $1,200. A 2,275-tonne stock fall maintained recent trends, and prices ended at $1,169, down $3.
The lead market was relatively unexciting throughout, and a dull kerb ended with three months at a little-changed $674/675 a tonne.
New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, but palladium extended its rally, as Russian supply problems continued to impact, traders said.
"Gold has been consolidating for the past three sessions, after spot gold fell below $350 last week and became oversold again," Pell Brothers COMEX floor trader Don Tierney said.
"Gold open interest fell further in this morning's open interest data, suggesting fund buying Monday was just shortcovering," he said.
COMEX April gold ended down $2.10 an ounce at $346.40, after trading a $349.20-3461.0 range.
In data released Tuesday, total open interest in COMEX gold futures fell 3,972 contracts Monday to 191,872 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $344.00/50, after fixing at $345.70 in London Tuesday afternoon, compared to the New York close Monday around $346.40/90.

Gold prices saw fresh three year lows last week, on more concern about central bank sales and a seasonal dip in demand during the Ramadan and Chinese New Year holidays, with a strong U.S. dollar limiting investor interest in gold also.
The decline in the gold price may be making some high-cost gold mines unprofitable though, analysts said.

The price of gold in South African rand was now at a nine month low as the South African rand stabilized after last year's sharp fall. "A sharp reversal of the fortunes of the (South African gold mining) industry is now in prospect because of the recent strengthening of the rand," industry consultant Edward Osborn of Edey, Rogers Pty Ltd in South Africa said.

"With capex (capital expenditure) brought into the picture, nearly half of the number of reporting mines (in South Africa), representing 2.45 pct of national production, operated at a loss (in the fourth quarter 1996)," he said.
CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with March finishing lower after setting a new contract low of $3.56-1/2 per bushel in early dealings, traders said.
Skepticism about a significant pickup in U.S. wheat exports despite a spate of light volume business overnight weighed on the March contract, they said.
Wheat closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with March down 3-3/4 at $3.57-3/4.

Crude oil prices fell on NYMEX, following a weaker heating oil market. March crude prices fell 11 cents a barrel to $24.04. Heating oil fell on talk of a major player having taken a large delivery. "This delivery could weigh on the physical market since there is already so much supply out there," said a dealer.
